title: Design and operation of a molten salt electrochemical cell
author: Consiglio, Carotti, et al.

steps.title: Clean all cell components
steps.instruction: Before first use, clean every material that will contact the molten salt (electrodes, thermowell, etc.) with ethanol and laboratory residue‑free wipes.

steps.title: Apply BN aerosol coating to Pt wires
steps.instruction: Cover electrode areas that must stay bare with tape, then spray BN aerosol onto the Pt wires in several very thin coats, allowing several minutes of drying between coats; remove the tape and inspect the coating to ensure it is thin, smooth and crack‑free; slide the BN tube over the electrode to protect against shorting; note that in reported tests the BN layer showed no deterioration when immersed in highly reduced FLiBe (FLiBe + LiH) at 600 °C for over 36 h.

substeps.instruction: Cover bare‑required electrode regions with tape.
Apply BN spray in multiple thin layers, waiting several minutes between applications.
Remove tape and visually inspect for a thin, smooth, crack‑free coating.
Slide the BN tube onto the electrode for additional short‑circuit protection.

steps.title: Clean electrodes between experiments if shorting occurs
steps.instruction: If shorting cannot be avoided, withdraw the Pt working and reference electrodes, remove the BN sleeves, clean the Pt wires in an ultrasonic bath with deionized water and nitric acid, polish with 1200‑grit sandpaper, then re‑apply the BN layer and BN sleeves as described above; replace the sleeve with a new one if it becomes too tarnished.

substeps.instruction: Withdraw Pt working and reference electrodes and remove their BN sleeves.
Place Pt wires in an ultrasonic bath containing deionized water and nitric acid to remove salt deposits, impurities, and the BN coating.
Polish the electrode surfaces with 1200‑grit sandpaper.
Re‑apply the BN aerosol coating and slide new BN sleeves onto the electrodes; use a fresh BN sleeve if the previous one is overly tarnished.
